audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL internals (EVM arithmetic, comparisons, trie operations, fork structure, gas/mana renaming, on-chain deposits) and CL logic (validator index reuse fork choice, light client P2P, weak subjectivity, proposer lookahead). Both layers and their interfaces are in scope.

misclassified_entities.reason: In spec_b0c87992, 'Consensus Layer' is listed as external entity for the Prague fork activation. When auditing both EL and CL, this is better modeled as 'CL via Engine API' to distinguish the interface from the component itself.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (newPayload, forkchoiceUpdated, fork activation signals)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT, but payload content (block data, fork activation) must be validated by EL. Derived from EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER in spec_b0c87992.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated public RPC. Transaction data and parameters are fully attacker-controlled. Covers EXT-USER from spec_b0c87992 and EXT-RPC-CLIENT from spec_b974c559.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peer can send arbitrary block data. Derived from EXT-PEER in spec_b0c87992.

trusted_external_entities.name: Staker via Deposit Transaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can submit deposit transactions. Deposit data (pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, signature) is attacker-controlled and must be fully validated. Derived from EXT-STAKER in spec_bcbc93ac.

trusted_external_entities.name: DoS Attacker via Deposit Spam
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Deposit contract calls (mass deposit submission for DoS)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker submitting maximum deposits per block to slow processing. Cost ~1000 ETH to delay by 1 second makes it economically difficult but not impossible. Derived from EXT-ATTACKER in spec_bcbc93ac.

trusted_external_entities.name: New Validator Deposit via Beacon Chain
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Validator deposit processing (index allocation in EIP-6914)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Deposits originate from EL and are processed by CL. The timing and targeting of deposits could be manipulated to exploit index reuse. Derived from EXT-NEW-VALIDATOR-DEPOSIT in spec_ae8092dc.

trusted_external_entities.name: Full Node via Light Client Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Full nodes publish light client updates over gossip. Light clients cannot fully trust any single publisher; updates must be validated via sync committee signatures. Derived from EXT-FULL-NODE in spec_b2c6a56e.

trusted_external_entities.name: Serving Peer via Light Client Req/Resp
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: GetLightClientBootstrap, LightClientUpdatesByRange, GetLightClientFinalityUpdate, GetLightClientOptimisticUpdate req/resp protocols
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Serving peers respond to light client queries. Responses contain fork-versioned SSZ data that must be validated before processing. Derived from EXT-SERVING-PEER in spec_b2c6a56e.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted Peer via SSZ Messages
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P network SSZ-encoded light client messages
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any peer can send SSZ-encoded messages. Fork version must be validated before deserialization to prevent type confusion attacks. Derived from EXT-UNTRUSTED-PEER in spec_b2c6a56e.

trusted_external_entities.name: Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint Provider
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Checkpoint sync endpoint (external API providing ws_state and ws_checkpoint)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Checkpoint providers are semi-trusted: they are explicitly chosen by the node operator and represent community consensus. However, a compromised provider could direct nodes onto an attacker-controlled fork. Derived from EXT-CHECKPOINT-PROVIDER in spec_b7dca68c.

trusted_external_entities.name: Long-Range Attacker via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Adversary presenting a conflicting chain forked from an old finalized checkpoint. Weak subjectivity mechanism defends against this within the WS period. Derived from EXT-ATTACKER in spec_b7dca68c.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via Effective Balance Grinding
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon chain validator operations (balance adjustments, RANDAO observation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validator attempting to manipulate effective balance after observing RANDAO to influence proposer selection. EIP-7917 lookahead mechanism defends against this. Derived from EXT-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR in spec_bff057a3.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Network (RANDAO Reveals)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RANDAO values are publicly revealed in block proposals. Any validator can observe them. The security relies on unpredictability at the time effective balances are set, not on secrecy. Derived from EXT-NETWORK in spec_bff057a3.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: EL must independently validate fork activation criteria (block number/timestamp). JWT authentication ensures channel integrity but fork parameters must be verified against local configuration.
Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, gas limit validation, balance sufficiency, EIP-2718 type envelope parsing.
Input parameters must be validated to prevent resource exhaustion during estimation. Malformed transaction parameters should be rejected before simulation.
Full block validation required: header validation, transaction execution, state root verification, receipt root verification. Malformed blocks must be rejected without crashing.

Deposit logs must be filtered by exact contract address (0x00000000219ab540356cbb839cbe05303d7705fa) and event signature hash. Data must be exactly 576 bytes. Field parsing is structural; cryptographic validation deferred to CL.

Economic cost of deposit spam (~1000 ETH per second of delay) provides primary defense. Maximum 8192 deposits per payload caps worst-case processing. BLS signature verification timing must be bounded.

Index reuse must atomically clear equivocation history via on_reused_index(). Attacker must not be able to time deposits to receive specific indices. is_reusable_validator() must enforce sufficient cooldown period.
Fork version must be validated before SSZ deserialization. Light client updates must be verified against sync committee signatures. Rate limiting via gossipsub scoring assumed.
Bootstrap data must be validated against known checkpoint. Fork-versioned SSZ type must match expected fork version for the requested slot. Malformed responses must be rejected.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: SSZ deserialization for light client messages
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Fork version must be determined from slot/epoch before selecting SSZ type. Deserialization with wrong type must fail safely without crashes or memory corruption. Messages at genesis fork version must be rejected.

Checkpoint root and epoch must be validated against chain state. Node must verify it is within the weak subjectivity period. If outside WS period, node must halt and require operator intervention for fresh checkpoint.
Conflicting chains must be rejected if they disagree with a valid WS checkpoint within the WS period. Node must track WS period expiry and refuse to sync if exceeded.

Effective balances must be frozen at epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1 before RANDAO for epoch N is known. Proposer schedule stored in state must be immutable once computed. Lookahead vector must be initialized correctly at fork activation.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: RANDAO seed retrieval for proposer computation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: RANDAO values must be unpredictable at the time effective balances are set. MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD provides the temporal separation. If RANDAO prediction advances, the security margin must be re-evaluated.
